notes: This filing says: "Since the business is mobile, we expect that you will run your BARK & MANE Franchised Business from your home and no site approval is required." No premises rent is modeled, because a category occupancy band would invent a lease the filing does not describe. Read that sentence as written — a filing saying MOST franchisees work from home is not telling you that you will — and confirm with the franchisor what space you would actually need.

underwriting.assessment: $250,000 liquid covers the $187,988 mid-point build-out without financing, though that leaves little working-capital cushion. At mid-cohort revenue, about $23,028/mo is left after fees, rent and debt service — cost of goods and labor still come out of that, and the cash ladder below subtracts them.

financialCondition.headline: The franchisor's statements don't show the distress signals we screen for — positive net worth and a clean audit. Still worth a quick confirmation against current figures.
body: What we found (2025-12-31, audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP): Net income of $17.60M on $145.47M of revenue — roughly 0.9x spent per $1 earned. Positive net worth of $432.60M. About 45% of liabilities is money owed to related parties — the entity is kept alive largely by insider loans, not profit. Cash of $20.07M against $48.49M of obligations due within a year (a current ratio of 0.92).

Why it matters to you: field support, training, technology, and marketing come out of the franchisor's budget. If outside funding slows, those are the first things to get cut. Home Franchise Concepts, LLC guarantees the franchisor's performance, which partly backstops this.

Verify before you commit: ask for the most recent interim (unaudited) financials and the current-year funding plan; ask whether the parent will sign a guarantee of performance; and cross-check Item 20 — unit closures, transfers, and terminations are the operational tell that corroborates financial stress.
aggravators: more due within a year than current assets to cover it
heavy dependence on related-party loans to stay funded
elevated unit closures (9 in the last year, about 5% of the system)
mitigants: the auditor issued a clean (unmodified) opinion and did not raise going-concern doubt
the parent guarantees the franchisor's performance
financialCondition.evidenceNote: Derived from the Item 21 / Exhibit F audited financials. Figures are extracted; all ratios and grading are computed. Confirm against the source statements and a CPA before relying on them.
